reasoning_content:
Installed. Next, install Node.js from NodeSource, and in parallel download the Elasticsearch 7.17.x tarball.

Actually, let's do the NodeSource install and the ES download in a single command (sequentially within one shell, but both within the 600-second budget). The ES 7.17.28 tarball is about 320MB. At the speed observed (2.4MB/s, which was a partial download test) it could take more than 2 minutes... Actually, the partial test showed a download speed of 2387605 bytes/s ≈ 2.3MB/s → 320MB would be about 140 seconds. Within budget, but let's run it in the background with nohup and poll it. Better yet: start the ES download in the background and, in the meantime, install Node.

action.command:
mkdir -p /opt/downloads && cd /opt/downloads && nohup curl -sS -o elasticsearch-7.17.28-linux-x86_64.tar.gz https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28-linux-x86_64.tar.gz > es_download.log 2>&1 &
echo "Download started in background, PID $!"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "mkdir -p /opt/downloads && cd /opt/downloads && nohup curl -sS -o elasticsearch-7.17.28-linux-x86_64.tar.gz https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28-linux-x86_64.tar.gz > es_download.log 2>&1 &\necho \"Download started in background, PID $!\"", "summary": "Start Elasticsearch 7.17.28 download in background", "security_risk": "HIGH"}
